A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Kaleidoscopic Scintillation Event Imaging by the same authors. The main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–I are readable and support comparison after matching relocated and renumbered figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original SPAD-camera experiments with a Co-60 source, localization simulations, and a regularization ablation, including results in Tables 1–2 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original hardware experiments, simulation comparisons, and appendix ablation results. These remain original empirical outcomes of the work.

M1.justification: The square-pyramid scintillator design, density-weighted Gaussian mixture model, regularized objective, weighted KMeans initialization, and EM optimization remain unchanged in Sections 3–4.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Co-60 experimental images and simulated scintillation events. PET and SPECT are newly named as application examples in the introduction, but neither is added to the evaluation.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the non-kaleidoscopic version of the authors' algorithm and the Noise-removing method [8]. Appendix G and Table 2 retain the same prior method with threshold values of 40, 80, and 120 pixels.

E3.justification: Acquisition, filtering, calibration, and evaluation procedures match. Both retain 4,379 experimental images, 1,606 cross-validation events, and simulations over 463 locations at three brightness levels, with the same noise model and error/resolution metrics.

E4.justification: The mirror-removal consistency analysis, regularization ablation in Appendix F, threshold sensitivity results in Appendix G, and qualitative examples are retained. Recolored Gaussian overlays do not introduce new analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same means, medians, standard deviations, and distribution histograms, and specify 100 simulated images per location and brightness level. No seed information, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are added.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2, histogram findings, and annotated experimental counts and positions match. For example, Table 1 retains kaleidoscopic 3D errors of 0.14, 0.16, and 0.29 mm at brightness levels 30, 20, and 10, respectively. The appendix ablation results also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3 removes the assertion that considering a square pyramid is 'without loss of generality,' modestly qualifying the stated theoretical scope. The mathematical models, equations, truncation derivation, and likelihood/gradient derivations in Appendices A, C, and I otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same claims about increased light collection, preserved spatial information, imaging theory, and 3D localization. The claims of improved simulated localization and sub-millimeter resolution are unchanged.

C2.justification: The introduction adds an explicit explanation that larger, thicker scintillators increase event probability while making 3D localization harder. Interpretations of the experimental results and the existing limitations concerning geometry, higher-order reflections, and multiple events remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v1 explicitly identifies a GitHub repository for code and data; v2 replaces that statement with a project-page link below the authors. This changes access guidance, without establishing any change in actual resource availability. Hardware specifications, calibration instructions, and algorithm parameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 37 references and substantive comparisons with earlier kaleidoscopic, stereo, plenoptic, and depth-from-defocus work are retained. The shortened description of reference [12] and added application examples do not materially change novelty or research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited prose and terminology edits, standardizes heading capitalization, renames Section 5 to Hardware Experiments and Section 6 to Simulations, and clarifies appendix references. It also changes author-contact presentation and adds a specific funding acknowledgment; the overall narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the overview, combines v1 Figures 2–3 into Figure 2, and consolidates appendix setup photographs into main-text Figure 4, omitting one setup view. Figures 5 and 11–13 distinguish events from reflections using red and blue; Figure 12 loses its pixel axes. These are targeted graphical refinements, while tables and histogram designs remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The event/reflection color distinction and labeled setup composite make the method and experimental examples easier to understand, while the scientific evidence remains intact. Removing Figure 12's pixel axes makes the calibration discussion less directly checkable, and code/data access labeling becomes less explicit. These modest drawbacks temper, but do not outweigh, the limited improvement in clarity.
